extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journalists, policymakers, and practitioners interested in civic information, media trust, free expression, and philanthropy-funded research
extracted.subtask_description: Overview page describing Knight Foundation’s commissioned research priorities, thematic series, and recent reports — highlighting focus areas such as civic information, free expression, asset manager diversity, and media/trust studies. Useful for researchers seeking to align proposals or understand the foundation’s research agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to understanding of informed and engaged communities
rubrics_metrics.description: We commission research that contributes to the broader understanding of informed and engaged communities, both now and in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioned research should focus on key thematic areas that contribute to ongoing conversations of significance to the foundation (i.e., should meaningfully advance understanding of civic information, engagement, or community dynamics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pew‑Knight Initiative objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Deepen our understanding of how Americans absorb civic information, form beliefs and identities, and engage in their communities (Pew Research Center and Knight Foundation partnership launched in 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research under this initiative should target the processes of information consumption, belief/identity formation, and civic engagement among Americans and be suitable for collaborative, large‑scale study with partner organizations like Pew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knight Free Expression Research Series — First Amendment focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight Foundation values the First Amendment, evident in our ongoing research on free expression since 2004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research in this series should examine free expression/First Amendment issues (historical trends, attitudes, policy impacts) and be positioned as part of a long‑running inquiry into speech rights and related societal dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and Society topical focus (book restrictions, campus speech, youth views)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics highlighted include Americans’ views on book restrictions in U.S. public schools, college student views on free expression and campus speech, and high schooler views on speech over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals or studies should address concrete manifestations of information and society tensions (e.g., book bans, campus speech controversies, youth attitudes) and connect findings to broader civic information concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knight Diversity of Asset Managers Research Series — transparency in asset manager use
rubrics_metrics.description: Research to foster transparency about the use of diverse owned asset managers; series originated after Knight changed investment practices starting in 2010 and includes higher education–focused reports (e.g., 2024 higher education releases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in this series should investigate diversity in asset management, reporting practices, and higher education endowment management, and aim to increase transparency and inform institutional investment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust, Media and Democracy research scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Study of media trust, news sustainability, and attitudes towards internet policy and technology; the project produced multiple reports and articles (2017–2022) documenting public attitudes and sector sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should examine public trust in media, factors affecting news sustainability, and related technology/internet policy attitudes; outputs are expected as reports/articles that contribute to public and academic discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on producing publicly useful reports and measurable impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust, Media and Democracy project produced 12 reports and 22 articles that received 900+ media mentions and 500+ academic citations — signaling emphasis on tangible, publicly consumable outputs and measurable influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funded or showcased by the foundation is expected to produce accessible reports/articles and ideally generate media coverage and academic engagement as indicators of impact.
